questions.q: What is the key structural limitation of a key-value store like Redis, per this lesson?
options: The database has no visibility into the internal structure of the stored value, so it can't query on the value's contents
It cannot store more than one value per key
It requires a fixed schema for every value, identical to a relational table
It cannot be used for caching or session storage
questions.explain: A key-value store treats the value as opaque — great for lookup-by-key, but you can't query on fields inside it the way you can with a document database.

questions.q: What genuinely distinguishes a document database like MongoDB from a plain key-value store?
options: Documents can be queried and indexed on their internal fields, not just retrieved by a single key
Document databases don't allow any querying at all, only key-based retrieval
Document databases require every document in a collection to share an identical schema
There is no real difference — 'document database' is just marketing language for key-value stores
questions.explain: MongoDB can query and index directly on fields inside a document, which a key-value store's opaque value cannot support.

questions.q: Why are column-family databases like Cassandra well suited to IoT telemetry and time-series logging, per this lesson?
options: They're built for massive write throughput across many distributed nodes with no single point of failure
They offer the most flexible ad hoc querying of any NoSQL model
They enforce strict relational schemas that guarantee data integrity
They are the simplest of the four models to design for
questions.explain: Cassandra's peer-to-peer, masterless architecture is optimized for extreme write scale, which is exactly what high-volume telemetry needs.

questions.q: What makes a graph database like Neo4j the honest right tool for fraud ring detection, per this lesson?
options: Relationships are stored as first-class objects, so traversals like friends-of-friends are fast local walks instead of chained, increasingly expensive JOINs
Graph databases store data in flat rows exactly like a relational table
Graph databases cannot represent connections between entities at all
Fraud detection requires no relationship traversal, just simple lookups
questions.explain: Tracing rings of connected accounts is exactly the kind of relationship traversal graph databases are structurally optimized for.

questions.q: Why does this course focus on document, multi-model, and graph databases rather than covering a standalone key-value or column-family store in depth?
options: Document and graph modeling require an ongoing design discipline that justifies deeper coverage, while key-value and standalone column-family stores solve narrower, simpler problems
Key-value and column-family databases are no longer used in production
This course considers key-value and column-family models inferior to document and graph models
Cosmos DB does not support any column-family or key-value style workloads
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this is about depth of design discipline needed, not a judgment that the other models are unimportant.
